title: Operator-stitched feedback brief: prioritized probe catalog
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a stitched, operator-centric roll-up of recent customer threads (support tickets, SRE pager notes, field CS transcripts) focused on how inference behavior shows up in production support. Goal: produce a short, actionable probe catalog (low, med, high effort) that engineering + product can pick from for Q1 planning.

How this doc was assembled:
- Pulled top 60 support threads tagged "latency", "auth-failure", "fallback-model" (2026-10 to 2026-11).
- Cross-referenced with two SLO incidents and three dedicated customer postmortems.
- Quick interviews: 4 CSM handoffs, 2 on-call SREs, 1 solutions-eng call.

Top operator pain themes (short):
1) Transient auth token failures cause cascade retries and cost spikes. Pattern: short-lived KMS refresh errors during high-write bursts -> client retries -> queueing spikes.
2) Silent model-fallbacks: customer apps observe content changes after automatic fallback to quantized variants; customers only notice because downstream business logic (e.g., entity extraction) regresses.
3) Cold KV cache priming for long-form chat sessions increases tail latency for first 3-5 user messages.
4) Observability gaps: customers can see request-level errors but not token-level cost attribution across retries — makes billing disputes hard.
5) Multi-region routing surprises: traffic cutover without explicit client pinning leads to subtle prompt-formatting differences across region-local model variants.

Representative excerpts (redacted):
- "We saw a 3x increase in billable tokens on a Friday afternoon, no clear root cause in our code — support pointed to cascading retries after an auth error." (Large ecom customer)
- "Changed subtly: our parser started missing dates after the model swap. Noticed after customers reported wrong event times." (SaaS scheduling customer)

Priority probe catalog (annotated, pragmatic):
LOW EFFORT (days to 2 wks):
- Auth retry guard: add server-side exponential backoff hint in error payloads and a short-lived circuit (60s) that collapses noisy client retries. Expected impact: reduce cascading retries and token churn. Owner: eng-infra (Samir). Effort: 3-5d. Risk: low.
- Billing debug flag: enable per-request retry-chain-id in logs and expose a one-click CSV export for CS to attach to customer tickets. Owner: obs (Jin). Effort: 2-4d.
- "Fallback transparency" opt-in header: on by default for canary users, adds a small header in responses when the runtime used a fallback variant. Allows quick detection without changing SDK. Owner: product-hosted-api. Effort: 1-2w.

MEDIUM EFFORT (2–6 wks):
- KV cache warm path: instrument a lightweight prefetch hint for chat sessions (client can send "estimated-turns"); runtime will optionally pre-warm KV for models that benefit. Expected latency win for first messages. Owner: serving-runtime + SDK. Effort: 3w. Risk: medium (cost trade-off).
- Token-level billing telemetry: wire a downstream token attribution pipeline so we can split cost across retries, prefetch, and fallback model tokens in billing dashboards. Owner: finance + obs. Effort: 4–6w.

HIGH EFFORT (quarter or more):
- Region-pin control plane: allow customers to pin model variant mapping and rollout windows per-tenant to avoid silent variant mismatches during regional failovers. Deep infra + legal implications (data residency). Owner: private-deployments + legal + platform.
- Model-compatibility evaluation runner: automated nightly checks that run a fixed evaluation set across primary + fallback variants and surface regression deltas linked to recent customer prompt seeds. Owner: applied-ml + optimize. Effort: multi-sprint.

Quick priority ranking (CS POV):
1) Auth retry guard + billing debug flag (LOW) — unblock immediate customer pain and reduces cost exposure.
2) Fallback transparency header (LOW) — reduces surprise/regression discovery time.
3) KV warm path (MED) — high visibility in latency-sensitive customers.
4) Token-level billing telemetry (MED) — necessary for billing disputes & trust.
5) Region-pin and compatibility runner (HIGH) — strategic, but longer runway.

Operational notes / constraints seen in threads:
- Many customers use SDKs that retry aggressively; short-lived 401/403 in a spike will cause avalanche. Ideally combine client hints + server-side collapse.
- Fallbacks are configured by routing policy: sometimes chosen for cost, sometimes latency. Customers rarely know why.
- Cache priming should be opt-in for high-throughput tenants to avoid cost regressions.
- Support often lacks a single artifact to hand engineers (hence CSV export suggestion).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How much additional cost will pre-warming KV introduce at scale? Need an estimate model from serving-runtime. (action: ask runtime team for simulation).
- What sensitivity threshold should trigger server-side retry collapse? 401 only? 5xx? (proposal: start with auth-only).
- Can billing telemetry be backfilled for recent incidents to help reconcile open disputes? (finance feasibility check).

Suggested immediate next steps (1–3 weeks):
1) Kick a "short fixes" ticket with infra + obs to implement auth retry guard + billing debug export (combine into single 2-week sprint). Draft ticket: JIRA:CS-9123.
2) Product to spec fallback transparency header and opt-in canary list. Small UX brief + SDK header doc. (owner: product-hosted-api).
3) Run a two-week litmus on KV warm path in staging with two pilot tenants and capture cost delta. (owner: serving-runtime).
4) Finance + obs to do a scoping call on token attribution pipeline and backfill feasibility.

Notes to self / CS handoff checklist (for playbook):
- When a ticket mentions "token spike": ask for request-ids, time windows, and attach the one-click CSV from billing debug flag.
- For suspected fallback regressions: collect two samples (pre-failure and post-failure) and file with applied-ml regression runner once available.
- If multi-region mismatch suspected: check tenant's routing policy and region pinning state; recommend explicit pinning for critical customers until region-pin control plane is available.

Appendix: quick estimates & heuristics used in prioritization:
- Low effort = <2 engineer-weeks cross-org (fast ROI, low infra churn).
- Medium = 2–6 weeks, requires cross-team integration and QA.
- High = multi-sprint + policy/legal review.

If you want, I can break the LOW/ MED items into JIRA-ready subtasks with acceptance criteria and test steps.

-- Ava
(updated 2026-12-03 after sync with on-call SRE and Jin on observability scope)
